Reference implementation (Python 3.12+):
```python
def min_max(values):
    if not values:
        raise ValueError("values must not be empty")
    low = high = values[0]
    for value in values[1:]:
        if value < low: low = value
        if value > high: high = value
    return low, high

assert min_max([4, -2, 7, 7]) == (-2, 7)
```
explanation: One pass maintains the minimum and maximum so far. Time O(n), auxiliary space O(1). An empty input is rejected explicitly.
